setting: all settings (inpatient, hospital outpatient, ASC, office)
estimand: primary female anti-incontinence sling placements, annual national all-payer
source: Free three-source transport. (1) CMS Medicare Physician & Other Practitioners PUF CY2024, HCPCS 57288: 25,179 Medicare FFS services nationally. (2) CHIA Massachusetts outpatient observation, all-payer, FY2013-2018: 39.8% of 1,142 sling procedures in women aged 65+. (3) CMS Medicare enrollment: MA penetration 54% in 2024 (32.8M of 61.2M), so FFS share = 0.46. national = 25,179 / (0.398 x 0.46).
notes: LOWER BOUND, and the direction is knowable. Observation-stay slings are those kept overnight and skew OLDER than the ambulatory sling population, so 39.8% likely OVERSTATES the 65+ share; dividing by an inflated share biases the national total DOWNWARD. No CI: the CMS PUF publishes counts without sampling error, and the age-share and FFS-share factors carry unquantified transport uncertainty rather than sampling uncertainty. Do not attach a nominal interval. CAVEATS: the 65+ age share is Massachusetts, standing in for national; MA penetration is the ALL-AGES overall figure, not age- or sex-specific (CMS/KFF publish no such breakdown), and it rises yearly -- 55% by 2026 -- so this factor must be re-looked-up whenever the PUF vintage changes. HCUP SASD would answer this directly but is licensed and unaffordable; every input here is free.
